title: Column Headings with Runovers

illustrates.quote: c. Column headings and their runovers are left-justified above their respective columns.

print.notes: Only one data row is shown in the print excerpt (a fragment of a larger table).
print.surroundingText: Follows 11.4.2.c; is followed immediately by 11.4.3 Complex Tables with Column and Sub-column Headings.
print.printFeatures: Bordered box; header row bold with a ruled line beneath it.

braille.notes: 'Potential Population' runs over two lines: 'Habitat Potential' appears on the heading's first line (left-justified over its own column, i.e. 'Habitat' over the Habitat-Unit column and 'Potential' over the Potential-Population column) and 'Species / Unit / Population' complete each heading on the second line — all column headings end together on that same (second) line per rule 11.4.1.d. No separation line appears until after both heading lines are complete.

uncertain: No bottom box rule ('gggg...') or trailing blank line appears in the .txt source for this example, unlike every other boxed example in this section (11-2, 11-3, 11-8); this was not independently re-checked against the physical page beyond the .txt and the single page image already reviewed, so it is recorded as a deliberately partial excerpt rather than a proven one.
resolution: No content differences beyond header-schema normalization.
